newsitem.title: USA: Continental Airlines investor along for the ride.
newsitem.headline: Continental Airlines investor along for the ride.

text.p: Continental Airlines' largest investor has no plans to sell his stake soon despite reports that Continental has held merger talks with rival Delta Air Lines Inc., a spokesman for the investor said Thursday.

"There is no specific timetable for exiting," said Owen Blicksilver, a spokesman for financier David Bonderman, who led a $450 million investment that helped bring Continental out of bankruptcy in 1993.
"They're still real happy with the investment."

Reports of merger talks were fuelled partly by speculation that Bonderman's group was seeking to sell its stake in Continental. Industry experts said Bonderman, whose group acquired the stake while Continental was in bankruptcy, may have been the driving force behind the talks.

Executives of Houston-based Continental said in a memo to employees on Wednesday that a merger was not imminent but stopped short of denying the carriers were in talks on a deal that would create the nation's largest airline. The New York Times and Wall Street Journal first reported the negotiations on Wednesday.
"(Bonderman) has said he sees Continental as a mid-term investment. He was probably the one to instigate this," Andy Deane, spokesman for the Air Lines Pilots Association at Delta, said Thursday.
Delta pilots met with management Wednesday but were given no details of any talks between the two airlines.
"We have no say in whether a merger occurs, but we're an integral part of the process when it comes to combining operations," Deane said.

Industry analysts said a merger of Delta, the nation's third-largest airline, with No. 5 Continental would create a powerful carrier with attractive routes and profitable hubs, and most likely spark more mergers in the industry.
The merged company would also be in a strong position to compete with rival American Airlines, which is in the process of seeking a broad alliance with British Airways.
Delta and Continental have declined to comment publicly, leading some analysts to speculate the talks were still in the early stages and may not lead to a deal.

In the memo to employees, Continental Chairman Gordon Bethune said he and other executives would not have exercised stock options recently "if we thought a merger was right around the corner." He also assured workers they would not be left behind if long-awaited consolidation in the industry forces Continental to seek a merger partner.

Bethune succeeded Bonderman in October as chairman of the airline, which has taken steps to help the investment group recoup some of its investment. Continental in November cashed out $50 million in warrants held by Bonderman's Air Partners L.P., which also has trimmed its stake in the airline to less than 10 percent from just above 10 percent.

The Ft. Worth, Texas-based investor has said his fund is a "medium-term" investor in Continental, which observers read to mean the partnership will remain intact for at least a few Once Bonderman begins looking for an exit, Continental would have several options short of selling the airline to help the investor cash out. "It's a partnership, and as such over time you do realise some gains from the partners when you can," Blicksilver said.

At the airline's annual meeting last June -- with talks of a USAir Group takeover swirling around the industry -- Bonderman said Continental was not for sale unless a USAir sale sparked an industrywide consolidation.
"Nobody in senior management or ownership of the company is contemplating a sale or merger of the airline, period," he said at the meeting, his last at the helm of Continental.

Bonderman does not need proceeds from a Continental sale to underwrite his latest ventures. His Texas Pacific Group, formed with partner James Coulter, last month launched a second buyout fund seeking to raise up to $1.5 billion.
Bonderman last month also was named chairman of Ireland's Ryanair after heading a consortium that acquired a 20 percent stake in the airline.
